intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type (SMDS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the GPX4 gene (138322) on chromosome 19p13.

checks.claim: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type (SMDS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the GPX4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our identification of truncating mutations in GPX4 in two families affected with SSMD supports the pathogenic role of mutated GPX4 in this very rare disease.
checks.explanation: Compound heterozygosity shown in one family; homozygosity in second family only inferred from carrier parents (child's DNA unavailable).

checks.claim: The GPX4 gene is located on chromosome 19p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the enzyme glutathione peroxidase 4 cause Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location not in abstract; it is standard gene nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type is a rare, usually neonatally lethal, autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia. Its main features are severe irregular metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, and abnormal iliac crests. Affected infants often have cardiorespiratory problems, including cardiac conduction defects or arrhythmias, and central nervous system malformations such as abnormal neuronal migration with a simplified gyral pattern. Most die within days to weeks of birth.

checks.claim: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type is a rare skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: in this rare congenital lethal skeletal dysplasia with unknown etiology
checks.explanation: The abstract calls SSMD a rare skeletal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type is usually lethal in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) is a neonatal lethal form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia

checks.claim: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
checks.evidence_quote: suggests that the Sedaghatian syndrome is an autosomal recessive trait with high gene frequency in Iranians
checks.explanation: The abstract proposes autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: A main feature of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is severe irregular metaphyseal chondrodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiological findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia (Sedaghatian type).
checks.explanation: Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is mentioned, but 'severe irregular' is not described in the abstract.

checks.claim: A main feature of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is mild limb shortening.
checks.evidence_quote: His skeletal abnormalities included mild rhizomelic shortness of his limbs
checks.explanation: The abstract states mild rhizomelic limb shortening.

checks.claim: A main feature of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is platyspondyly.
checks.evidence_quote: His skeletal abnormalities included mild rhizomelic shortness of his limbs and platyspondylyl
checks.explanation: Platyspondyly is described.

checks.claim: A main feature of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is abnormal iliac crests.
checks.evidence_quote: platyspondylyl and "laciness" of the iliac wings
checks.explanation: Lacy iliac wings correspond to abnormal iliac crests.

checks.claim: Infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia often have cardiorespiratory problems.
checks.evidence_quote: Both died at three days of cardio-respiratory insufficiency
checks.explanation: Both infants had cardiorespiratory insufficiency.

checks.claim: Infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia often have cardiac conduction defects or arrhythmias.
checks.evidence_quote: platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities

checks.claim: Infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia often have central nervous system malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: central nervous system malformations might be a major component of the disorder
checks.explanation: The abstract says CNS malformations may be a major component of the disorder.

checks.claim: Central nervous system malformations in Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia include abnormal neuronal migration with a simplified gyral pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Our case highlights the possibility for neuronal migration abnormalities in Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract reports neuronal migration abnormality (pachygyria) in one case and calls it a possibility, not an established feature.

checks.claim: Most infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia die within days to weeks of birth.
checks.evidence_quote: Although all previously reported cases died within 4 days of life, our patient survived 161 days.
checks.explanation: Abstract supports death within days for previous cases; 'weeks' is not stated, and this patient survived months.

paragraphs.text: Sedaghatian (1980) described a lethal congenital metaphyseal chondrodysplasia in sibs. The disorder was later named after him.

checks.claim: Sedaghatian (1980) described a lethal congenital metaphyseal chondrodysplasia in sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: This is a report of two brothers, born within a year of each other, with a similar skeletal disorder of severe congenital metaphyseal involvement
checks.explanation: The title calls it a congenital lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, and the abstract reports it in two brothers.

checks.claim: The disorder described by Sedaghatian (1980) was later named after him.
checks.explanation: Later naming of the disorder after the author is not addressed by this paper.

paragraphs.text: Later reports described more affected infants with the same radiographic picture: severe irregular metaphyseal changes in the long bones, mild shortening of the limbs, flattened vertebral bodies, and irregular, lacy iliac crests. Many of these infants had cardiac arrhythmias or heart block, respiratory insufficiency, and brain malformations, including cortical dysplasia with a simplified gyral pattern and abnormalities of the corpus callosum. Most died in the neonatal period.

checks.claim: Later reports described additional infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia who had severe irregular metaphyseal changes in the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiological findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia (Sedaghatian type).
checks.explanation: One infant with metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is reported; 'severe irregular' changes in long bones are not detailed in the abstract.

checks.claim: Later-reported infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had mild shortening of the limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: In 1987 Optiz et al. described another Iranian infant with a similar perinatal course and roentgenograms.
checks.explanation: The later-reported infant had 'similar' radiographs to the index case, which had mild limb shortening. Limb shortening is not stated explicitly for the later cases.

checks.claim: Later-reported infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had flattened vertebral bodies.
checks.evidence_quote: In 1987 Optiz et al. described another Iranian infant with a similar perinatal course and roentgenograms.
checks.explanation: Platyspondyly is implied only through the 'similar roentgenograms'. It is not stated explicitly for the later cases.

checks.claim: Later-reported infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had irregular, lacy iliac crests.
checks.evidence_quote: In 1987 Optiz et al. described another Iranian infant with a similar perinatal course and roentgenograms.
checks.explanation: Lacy iliac wings are described for the index case. For the later infant they are implied only through the 'similar roentgenograms'.

checks.claim: Many infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had cardiac arrhythmias or heart block.
checks.evidence_quote: congenital atrioventricular block
checks.explanation: One patient had heart block. The abstract gives no evidence that many infants had it.

checks.claim: Many infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had respiratory insufficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: experienced recurrent cyanotic episodes within a few hours of delivery
checks.explanation: Cyanotic episodes in one infant are suggestive, but the abstract does not explicitly state respiratory insufficiency.

checks.claim: Many infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had cortical dysplasia with a simplified gyral pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebral imaging revealed absence of the corpus callosum and marked frontotemporal pachygyria.
checks.explanation: Pachygyria (a simplified gyral pattern) is reported in a single case, not in many.

checks.claim: Many infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia had abnormalities of the corpus callosum.
checks.evidence_quote: suggests a novel association of the disorder with agenesis of the corpus callosum
checks.explanation: Corpus callosum absence is reported in this one case and called novel, so it does not support 'many'.

checks.claim: Most later-reported infants with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia died in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: Although all previously reported cases died within 4 days of life, our patient survived 161 days.
checks.explanation: Previous cases died within 4 days, but this paper's patient survived 161 days, beyond the neonatal period.

paragraphs.text: The disorder affected sibs born to unaffected parents, sometimes in consanguineous families, which is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. The finding of biallelic GPX4 mutations confirmed this pattern.

checks.claim: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia affected sibs born to unaffected parents.
checks.evidence_quote: The occurrence in children of both sexes in one instance, born to normal parents who were first cousins
checks.explanation: Affected sibs were born to normal parents.

checks.claim: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia occurred in some consanguineous families.
checks.evidence_quote: This infant was born to first cousins, suggesting an autosomal recessive single gene defect.
checks.explanation: One affected infant was born to first cousins.

checks.claim: The familial pattern of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: This infant was born to first cousins, suggesting an autosomal recessive single gene defect.
checks.explanation: Consanguinity is presented as suggesting autosomal recessive inheritance, which fits the claim that the pattern is 'consistent with' it.

checks.claim: The finding of biallelic GPX4 mutations confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our identification of truncating mutations in GPX4 in two families affected with SSMD supports the pathogenic role of mutated GPX4
checks.explanation: Biallelic mutations found (one de novo), but the abstract does not explicitly state that they confirm AR inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2014) used exome sequencing in families with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and found biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the GPX4 gene, which encodes glutathione peroxidase-4. The mutations were predicted to truncate the protein.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2014) used exome sequencing in families with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing of a child affected with SSMD and her unaffected parents identified two rare variants in GPX4.
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing in only one family; the second family was studied by Sanger sequencing.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2014) found biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the GPX4 gene in families with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our identification of truncating mutations in GPX4 in two families affected with SSMD
checks.explanation: Biallelic mutations shown in one family; in the second the child was untested and the genotype was inferred from carrier parents.

checks.claim: The GPX4 gene encodes glutathione peroxidase-4.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the enzyme glutathione peroxidase 4 cause Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.

checks.claim: The GPX4 mutations found by Smith et al. (2014) in Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia were predicted to truncate the protein.
checks.evidence_quote: with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4

paragraphs.text: GPX4 is a selenoprotein that reduces lipid hydroperoxides in membranes and protects cells from lipid peroxidation, including ferroptotic cell death. Loss of GPX4 activity is thought to underlie the skeletal, cardiac, and neurologic features of the disorder.

checks.claim: GPX4 is a selenoprotein.
checks.explanation: Selenoprotein status not mentioned.

checks.claim: GPX4 reduces lipid hydroperoxides in membranes.
checks.evidence_quote: protects cells against membrane lipid peroxidation
checks.explanation: Reduction of lipid hydroperoxides not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: GPX4 protects cells from lipid peroxidation, including ferroptotic cell death.
checks.evidence_quote: protects cells against membrane lipid peroxidation
checks.explanation: Ferroptosis not mentioned.

checks.claim: Loss of GPX4 activity is thought to underlie the skeletal, cardiac, and neurologic features of Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings highlight the importance of this enzyme in development of the cardiac, nervous, and skeletal systems.
